expectations.text: Gives every queue item an action that ships alone and improves the docs by itself
expectations.evidence: Every row in the remediation queue is a concrete, independently shippable change, and the table even carries a dedicated "Reader need fixed" column stating the standalone reader benefit per row (row 1 "onboarding stops handing out two different IAM roles"; rows 4–9 "procedure and lookup table stop competing for the same scroll"; row 10 "IaC adopters get a supported path instead of a ticket"). No row is a scaffold, an empty-section creation, an inventory-only step, or a big-bang restructure — the nav-coupling check and the week-6 re-score are deliberately kept outside the queue. expectations.text: Gives every queue item an action that ships alone and improves the docs by itself
expectations.evidence: Most items are deliberately re-scoped into standalone, no-breakage units: item 1 rewrites one canonical page and stubs the duplicate ("Neither URL gets deleted"); item 3 is a brand-new page/URL with "no breakage risk" and is itself split into draft → SME validation → publish; item 4 either flips a nav field per page or, in the URL-baked case, "Cross-link, don't relocate" so the old URL survives; item 5 keeps how-to steps on the existing URL and spins the option table onto a new reference page, at ~1-1.5 hr/page so each page ships on its own. Deduction: item 2's fallback branch produces no docs
